title: Signature Canvas Fingerprint Poisoning
description: Adds imperceptible random noise to HTML canvas readback so every session yields a different image hash while the picture looks identical to the user. It works by wrapping CanvasRenderingContext2D.getImageData and HTMLCanvasElement.toDataURL with a per-session seeded perturber that flips a few low-order pixel bits. Brave calls this farbling, and the CanvasBlocker extension offers the same protection. This is a Signature original authored by Justin Addam Higgins — an original technique in the Signature system, clearly labeled Signature and not presented as public record.
key_mechanisms: Hook getImageData/toDataURL with a per-session seeded PRNG
Perturb low-order pixel bits below visual thresholds
Rotate the seed per session so hashes never repeat

title: Signature User-Agent Client Hints Reduction

title: Signature WebGL Renderer String Masking

title: Signature TLS ClientHello Normalization
description: Reorders and trims TLS ClientHello extensions and cipher suites to match the most common fingerprint on the network, defeating JA3-style passive identification. Tools like uTLS parrot popular clients (Chrome, Firefox) byte-for-byte, and proxies can rotate the parroted profile per connection. It must track real client updates or the mimicry itself becomes a fingerprint. key_mechanisms: Parrot a popular client's extension order and GREASE values

title: Signature WebRTC Local IP Leak Prevention

Setting the IP handling policy to disable non-proxied UDP forces all candidates through the proxy, and binding the interface achieves the same for full-tunnel setups.
